summary.body:
Five signals converge on a single tailwind: AI's consumer-subsidy era is collapsing into enterprise-grade billing, and every door it closes opens a bigger one for Krish's ventures. The story is unmistakeable — Anthropic, Google, and Meta are blocking third-party AI subscriptions because autonomous agents run continuous loops that burn through $200-400/month in compute behind every $20 Claude Pro. Microsoft lost $80 per user on Copilot. The vendor IPO timer is driving a market-wide repricing that transforms AI cost governance from a niche concern into a board-level mandate overnight. The optimist sees the play: the moment surprise AI bills land in CFO inboxes, MindMaker becomes the call they make.

GitHub's Spec Kit crossed 100k stars with 206 contributors and 30+ agent integrations — MIT-licensed — as the industry's collective realization that 'vibe coding' creates hidden fragility that compounds inside two weeks. Keith Shields of Designli quantified it: non-technical founders who shipped fast with AI are roughly a fortnight from discovering their technical debt. The engineering governance market is forming in real time, and Felix has a standing invitation to own it. The 'vibe code rescue' audit package writes itself.

Anthropic's Claude for Small Business — 15 pre-built workflows, QuickBooks through DocuSign — compresses the easy consulting wedge. This is not bad news. It is a market-clearing event. The bottom-feeders who sold 'I'll set up Claude for your QuickBooks' are out. Vertical specialists with regulated-industry depth, messy integration chops, and the ability to navigate compliance complexity inherit a cleaner, less crowded field. MindMaker's consulting tier gets sharper by market force.

The macro thesis: every AI market transition — pricing from seats to usage, coding from prompt-and-pray to spec-and-ship, consulting from general to vertical — creates a governance gap. Governance gaps are where premium advisory revenue lives. Krish has the rare advantage of seeing all three transitions simultaneously and building the audit, maturity, and regulated-industry packages before the market widely registers the openings. The window in each case is measured in months, not years.

top_3_actions.action: Ship the AI cost audit + predictive budgeting service for finance teams facing vendor price transitions — the first vendor IPO that triggers repricing is the lead generator
Launch a fixed-price 'vibe code rescue' audit package for non-technical founders hitting their 2-week technical debt wall — upsell to full governance engagement
Refresh consulting packaging to emphasize regulated-industry depth (healthcare, legal, financial services) as Claude SMB commoditizes basic automation — retire any 'basic AI automation' positioning

summary.blockers: No blockers. Krish has clear runway. Every market signal reads as an asymmetric opportunity — the transitions are happening faster than the market can adapt, and MindMaker's positioning sits at the inflection point of all three.
